scope: Move completed one-shot STT transport cleanup off the PTT reply critical path within the existing SttStage. No SDK, provider protocol, EOT, intent strategy or mode-owner changes.
production_change: SttStage keeps one owned close task. Successful streaming recognition returns after the same pre-existing END_OF_SPEECH/iterator completion boundary. A lock serializes one-shot recognition; subsequent streaming or offline recognition joins prior cleanup before opening/using another stream. Shutdown joins cleanup before plugin shutdown. Failed/cancelled recognition still awaits close, and shielding preserves cleanup ownership under repeated cancellation.
lifecycle_contract: Production PTT already cancels and joins turn tasks before stage shutdown. Direct callers shutting down during recognition wait for it; no new recognition timeout was introduced. There is at most one pending stream-close task per stage, not an unbounded background task queue.
tradeoff: A rapid next PTT release can still wait for unfinished prior cleanup. This preserves shared-connection isolation and bounds cleanup concurrency. Transport work is overlapped with response generation, not removed or forcibly timed out.
unchanged: PTT press/release/tap-to-stop and commit ownership, full/half-duplex continuous STT stream paths, LiveKit scheduler, ASR result-selection boundary, dependencies and shared settings.

comparison_method: Existing test_real_speech_to_real_reply with real configured Bailian ASR/TTS and direct LLM, generic normal_ask_intro.wav, ffmpeg atempo .7/1/1.4, brief instruction and explicit experimental 96-token cap. Same updated code for both variants: a test-process wrapper restores waiting for stream cleanup before returning text in the synchronous control. This is not a separate historical production checkout run. Order alternates for normal speed. Actual SDK/production PTT pipeline and memory sink.
interpretation: All six real service runs passed their transcription, reply-audio and usage assertions. Task-finished to returned text is 1189.8-1197.8 ms in synchronous controls and 0.3 ms in all three updated runs. WebSocket close still takes 1166.5-1535.2 ms in updated runs and is awaited by lifecycle. This supports removing the measured cleanup dependency, not reducing the recognition or network duration.
measurement_limits: Each speed/variant once, no P95 or production SLO; total release-to-first-audible differences include cloud variability.
Local regressions were running during some provider calls; do not interpret end-to-end differences as a strictly isolated performance benchmark.
Real service reply sink is in memory, not RTC/speaker. Full-duplex EOT/intent defects remain unresolved.
The prior PTT 45-second whole-reply timeout is not claimed fixed by this change.
